brief.prose: The plan for Moore and Nussmeier's offense was Tyson as a downfield weapon opposite Chris Olave, but an Aug. 13 hamstring strain (joint practice vs Jacksonville) has put real time on the shelf, with NFL Media pegging recovery at roughly two months and the team acknowledging he could open on IR (a minimum four-game absence). Moore blamed a foot-slip rather than a recurrence, but this is Tyson's fourth hamstring issue in four years. New Orleans has worked out Chase Claypool and Josh Reynolds as insurance. For redraft this is a fade: he misses the opening month, so he's a bench stash for later upside, not an early-season contributor.
brief.rationale: Two-month hamstring with possible IR; a redraft fade who misses the opening month, worth only a bench stash for later upside.

13286.name: Jadarian Price

brief.prose: Seattle's first-round rookie and the expected Week-1 lead back with Kenneth Walker gone and Zach Charbonnet likely to miss the start (still on PUP). The lower-body soreness that cost him a week and a half has cleared: he returned to full practice Aug. 18, and beat consensus (Gregg Bell) has him as the Week 1 lead. He sat the preseason as a precaution. A high-upside rookie with a path to real early volume in a scheme that spreads touches; the receiving role and goal-line work (6-point TDs) give him half-PPR RB2 upside the ADP may still lag. Recheck when Charbonnet is activated.
brief.rationale: Rookie back to full practice and the projected Week-1 lead with Charbonnet on PUP; real early volume plus receiving/goal-line work make him an underpriced RB2 upside play.

13287.name: Jeremiyah Love

brief.prose: Arizona is running a true rotation, not a lead-back handoff: in the opener Tyler Allgeier out-snapped rookie Jeremiyah Love 44-32 (NBC's box score has it 41-32) and out-touched him 19-13, with Love getting 11 carries for 41 yards and a first-drive touchdown, plus two catches for 9 yards, and Allgeier taking the clock-killing work. Head coach Mike LaFleur said game flow drove the split and that Love was not on a snap count, then on Sept. 18 said the two 'are going to rotate' and that he would not call it an expanded role for Love in Week 2 against Seattle. The ankle is no longer the story (he is off the injury report), so the ceiling now depends on whether the hot-hand approach tilts toward the third overall pick as his conditioning builds; until touch counts move, treat this as a committee with the higher upside on Love's side.
brief.rationale: The head coach says the split is a rotation with no expanded role coming, which a board that prices Love as the lead back has probably not absorbed.

13294.name: Makai Lemon

brief.prose: A first-round rookie drafted to help replace A.J. Brown (traded to New England), but the path to early snaps is murkier than the pedigree suggests. A hamstring cost him two weeks; he returned limited on Aug. 20 and is racing to catch up on the install before Week 1. Beyond DeVonta Smith (the focal point), Philadelphia also added veterans Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Dontayvion Wicks, so the WR2 job is crowded. The half-PPR upside is real long-term, but the injury and veteran competition make him a stash/late dart in redraft, not an immediate contributor.
brief.rationale: High-pedigree rookie back from a hamstring but behind on the install and buried in a veteran-added room; a redraft stash, not a Week 1 contributor.

events.headline: Broncos' J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman all take part in Wednesday practice despite injuries
events.detail: Denver's backfield was banged up coming out of Week 2: Dobbins left the Jacksonville game with a hamstring issue (the team also cited cramps), RJ Harvey is recovering from a hamstring injury and rookie Jonah Coleman has a sprained ankle. All three were on hand when Wednesday's practice opened ahead of Sunday night against the Rams. Denver also worked out three free-agent backs this week.
events.so_what: Better news than the injury list implied, but participation levels through Friday decide who carries the load Sunday night. Until then this backfield is a committee with health questions on every name, so none of the three is a confident start.
